source_refs.note: Exercise 4.2, Question 24: book p. 134 (Q2-Q25 general solutions and IVPs); answer key p. 303 (keys numbered 2-29)

blocks.text: As printed: Solve the initial value problem \(\left(y + \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}\right)dy - x\,dy = 0\); \(y = 0\) when \(x = 0\).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Two misprints. (1) The equation contains \(dy\) twice; the first must be \(dx\): \(\left(y + \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}\right)dx - x\,dy = 0\). As printed it would only say \(\left(y + \sqrt{x^2 + y^2} - x\right)dy = 0\), which is not the intended homogeneous equation. (2) The condition \(y = 0\) when \(x = 0\) cannot fix the constant: at \(x = 0\) the equation \(\frac{dy}{dx} = \frac{y + \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}}{x}\) is not defined, every solution curve \(y = \frac{Cx^2}{2} - \frac{1}{2C}\) meets \(x = 0\) at \(y = -\frac{1}{2C} \neq 0\), and the general solution \(y + \sqrt{x^2 + y^2} = Cx^2\) gives \(0 = 0\) at \((0, 0)\) for every \(C\). The key's answer \(y + \sqrt{x^2 + y^2} = x^2\) is the curve through \((1, 0)\), so we solve with \(y = 0\) when \(x = 1\).

blocks.prompt: 24 Solve the initial value problem \(\left(y + \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}\right)dx - x\,dy = 0\) [printed with \(dy\) in place of the first \(dx\)]; \(y = 0\) when \(x = 1\) [printed as \(x = 0\); see the correction above].
blocks.explanation:
The printed equation needs one correction (\(dx\) for the first \(dy\)); then every term has degree 1, so it is homogeneous.
The printed condition at \(x = 0\) cannot fix the constant; we use \(y = 0\) when \(x = 1\), which gives the key's answer.
Plan: \(y = vx\), separate, integrate \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{1 + v^2}}\), put back \(v\), then apply the condition.
steps:
Given: \(\left(y + \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}\right)dx - x\,dy = 0\), \(y = 0\) when \(x = 1\) (corrected).
To find: the particular solution.
Method: Homogeneous equation (Section 4.2.2): \(y = vx\); then the initial condition fixes \(C\). The initial point has \(x = 1 > 0\), so we work with \(x > 0\).

Write \(\frac{dy}{dx}\)
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{y + \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}}{x}\]
Why: every term (\(y\), \(\sqrt{x^2 + y^2}\), \(x\)) has degree 1, so the right side depends only on \(y/x\).

Substitute \(y = vx\)
\[\sqrt{x^2 + v^2x^2} = x\sqrt{1 + v^2}\]
\[v + x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = v + \sqrt{1 + v^2}\]
\[x\dfrac{dv}{dx} = \sqrt{1 + v^2}\]
Why: \(\sqrt{x^2} = x\) because \(x > 0\); then \(v\) cancels.

Separate and integrate
\[\int \dfrac{dv}{\sqrt{1 + v^2}} = \int \dfrac{dx}{x}\]
\[\ln\left(v + \sqrt{1 + v^2}\right) = \ln x + \ln C\]
\[v + \sqrt{1 + v^2} = Cx\]
Why: standard integral \(\int \frac{dv}{\sqrt{v^2 + 1}} = \ln\left|v + \sqrt{v^2 + 1}\right|\); here \(v + \sqrt{1 + v^2} > 0\), so no modulus, and \(C > 0\).

Put back \(v = y/x\) (general solution)
\[\dfrac{y}{x} + \dfrac{\sqrt{x^2 + y^2}}{x} = Cx\]
\[y + \sqrt{x^2 + y^2} = Cx^2\]
Why: \(\sqrt{1 + y^2/x^2} = \frac{\sqrt{x^2 + y^2}}{x}\) for \(x > 0\); multiply by \(x\).

Use \(y = 0\) when \(x = 1\)
\[0 + \sqrt{1 + 0} = C(1)^2\]
\[C = 1\]
\[y + \sqrt{x^2 + y^2} = x^2\]
Why: put the initial point into the general solution.

Explicit form
\[\sqrt{x^2 + y^2} = x^2 - y\]
\[x^2 + y^2 = x^4 - 2x^2y + y^2\]
\[y = \dfrac{x^2 - 1}{2}\]
Why: square both sides; \(y^2\) cancels, then divide by \(2x^2\).

Why the printed condition fails
In general \(\sqrt{x^2 + y^2} = Cx^2 - y\) gives
\[y = \dfrac{Cx^2}{2} - \dfrac{1}{2C}\]
At \(x = 0\) this is \(y = -\frac{1}{2C} \neq 0\), so no solution curve passes through \((0, 0)\).
Why: this is why the condition must be given at a point with \(x \neq 0\).

Check
For \(y = \frac{x^2 - 1}{2}\):
\[x^2 + y^2 = \left(\dfrac{x^2 + 1}{2}\right)^2\]
so \(y + \sqrt{x^2 + y^2} = x^2\) and \(\frac{y + \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}}{x} = x = \frac{dy}{dx}\) \(\checkmark\); \(y(1) = 0\) \(\checkmark\)
Why: the curve satisfies both the equation and the condition.
blocks.final_answer: \(y + \sqrt{x^2 + y^2} = x^2\), i.e. \(y = \frac{x^2 - 1}{2}\) (with the corrected condition \(y = 0\) when \(x = 1\))

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints this answer as number 28, not 24. The Exercise 4.2 keys are numbered 2 to 29 for 25 questions (key 2 answers Question 1, and the extra keys 15, 19 and 27 match no printed question), so look for this answer under 28. Its answer \(y + \sqrt{x^2 + y^2} = x^2\) is correct for the corrected problem (condition \(y = 0\) when \(x = 1\)).
